title: Arthur Keith Was the First to Describe What Is Now Known as Koch’s Triangle: The Building of the Triangular Locus of the Atrioventricular Node from Todaro to Tandler
content: Purpose: To show the developments that culminated with the eponym   Koch’s triangle -- the fibrous attachment of septal tricuspid leaflet, aperture of the coronary sinus and the tendon linking the inferior vena cava valve   to the  central fibrous body-   and how it was a construct  of several   anatomists. Methods: The literature is reviewed centering in the discovery  of the  atrioventricular node by Sunao Tawara (January 1906), its previous announcement by Tawara’s mentor Ludwig Aschoff (1905) as well as in the contributions of the authors that described the other components of the triangular locus.   Results :Tawara described  the atrioventricular  node and   its  relations with fibrous attachment of septal tricuspid leaflet and ostium of the coronary sinus. The first description assembling all components was  due to Arthur Keith (March1906). Keith was also the first to consider the triangular locus as useful landmark for identifying the atrial  structures of the conduction system discovered by  Tawara and Wilhelm His Jr (1893).. Conclusion: The triangular locus of the atrioventricular node  was a construct of several exceptional anatomists: The contributions of  keith in this topic   has been   particularly overlooked. The triangular locus of atrioventricular node or triangle of atrioventricular node are more instructive   and impartial   names.
